problem: For the function $f(x,y)=\frac{x}{y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(0,2).$
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)\cdot (y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{(y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x}{(y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{(y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(0,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(0,2)} & =\frac{2+\operatorname{sin}⁡0-0\operatorname{cos}⁡0}{(2+\operatorname{sin}⁡0)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2+0}{(2+0)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
